en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on the Great Chariot (Mahārathavagga)
9. The Second Mansion of the Needle:
“High is this mansion with its jeweled pillars, extending twelve yojanas in every direction.”
Seven hundred lofty gabled chambers,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with silver,
are there; therein you eat, drink, and enjoy.
Divine lutes resound with lovely tones;
here are the five divine qualities of sensual pleasure,
and women adorned in gold dance.
“By what means do you have such a complexion...
[and so on] ...and your complexion illuminates all directions?”
Thus that son of the gods was delighted...
[as before] ...the fruit of which deed this is.
“In a former birth, when I was among humans in the human world,
I saw a stainless bhikkhu.”
To him, whose mind was serene and undisturbed,
I, with a clear heart, gave a needle with my own hands.
"Because of that, my complexion is such as this...
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
The second Sūcivimāna, the ninth.
